statement: For independent standard Gaussian vertex weights on the n-vertex up/right free-endpoint path triangle, h_n(t)=E|P_n(g) intersect P_n(g^t)| is nonincreasing; Var(M_n)=integral e^(-t)h_n(t)dt. If h_n(n^(-alpha))<=C n^(1-delta), alpha,delta>0 fixed, then Var(M_n)<=(1+C)n^(1-min(alpha,delta)).

statement: In L1's Gaussian model, let q_v=P(v in P_n) and a(t)=tanh(t/2). Gaussian hypercontractivity implies h_n(t)<=sum_v q_v^(1+a(t)).
proof_or_counterexample: LEMMAS.md L2 applies the Gaussian semigroup inequality; no independence between site indicators is used.
remaining_gap: This upper-bound certificate is too large to give polynomial improvement, as L3 shows.

statement: For any q_v>=0 on Lambda_n with sum_{i+j=k}q_v=1 per layer k=0,...,n-1, B_n(t)=sum_v q_v^(1+tanh(t/2))>=n^(1-tanh(t/2)), and integral e^(-t)B_n(t)dt>=(n-1)/log n. At every t=n^(-alpha), alpha>0 fixed, B_n(t)/n tends to 1. Thus this direct per-site hypercontractivity certificate cannot certify O(n^(1-epsilon)) variance for any fixed epsilon>0.
assumptions: Exactly k+1 possible vertices on layer k
q_v are nonnegative with mass one on each layer
Only the unweighted per-site hypercontractive envelope is being assessed

source.basis: Chatterjee Lemma 4.1 plus finite-layer Jensen inequality

proof_or_counterexample: LEMMAS.md L3; Jensen gives B>=sum_{k=1}^n k^(-a)>=n^(1-a); u=e^(-t) and a<=(1-u) give integrated lower bound. This is NOT a lower bound on actual overlap or actual variance.
remaining_gap: Find a stronger joint-geometric coupled-overlap estimate; source problem remains unproved.

statement: Conditionally on Var(F_n)=n^(2chi+o(1)) and chi=2xi-1, a power bound Var(F_n)<=C n^(1-epsilon) requires xi<=3/4-epsilon/4; xi<1 is insufficient.
assumptions: Both exponent existence and the stated KPZ relation are assumed, not proved for polymers

source.quote: so a power improvement needs a quantitative transversal-fluctuation bound xi < 1 with an explicit gap

proof_or_counterexample: LEMMAS.md L4; 2chi=4xi-2, and xi=4/5 yields variance exponent 6/5.
